A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same regression framework and RG-Wormhole application. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations, point-cloud classification, distance-approximation benchmarks, and RG-Wormhole experiments in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds classical-method comparisons, class-distribution transfer tests, and fitted-coefficient analyses in Appendices B.6–B.8.

M1.justification: Equation 11 adds a factor of 1/K to each constrained-model sum, changing the stated combination of multiple lower/upper-bound predictors from summation to averaging. The unconstrained estimator, K=1 estimator, predictor families, and RG-Wormhole procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The existing dataset and task suite is retained. Appendix B.7 adds point-cloud scenarios that fit on within-class pairs and evaluate between classes, and vice versa. The scenario expansion is clear, although the text names ShapeNetV2 while Figures 21–22 name ModelNet40.

E2.justification: Appendix B.6 and Tables 5–6 introduce evaluated Sinkhorn and Linear OT comparators for runtime and approximation quality. v1 compared approximation primarily against Wormhole and evaluated individual sliced metrics elsewhere; these classical methods were not evaluated comparators. This substantially broadens the comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols include inference timing from 1 to 19,900 pairs, Sinkhorn tuning over three regularization values and 500/1,000 iterations, exclusion of RG calibration cost from inference timing, and class-restricted training/testing in B.7. Existing Wormhole hyperparameters are retained. Some new settings remain inconsistent: B.6 specifies 5,000 test pairs, whereas Table 6 specifies 10,000.

E4.justification: Appendix B.7 adds distribution-shift tests between within-class and between-class pairs. Appendix B.8 adds constrained and unconstrained coefficient analyses across four datasets, extending v1's Gaussian dimensionality analysis. These address new questions about transfer robustness and whether fitted weights generalize across datasets.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten seeds for Gaussian simulations and retain the same uncertainty-reporting format for classification results. The added comparisons and coefficient plots introduce no stated confidence intervals, significance tests, or new repeated-run reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 and Figures 21–30 add runtime, approximation, transfer, and coefficient results. For example, Table 5 reports RG-s inference time of 21.408 seconds versus Linear OT's 92.134 seconds for 200 shapes. Existing constrained-model results also change: Table 2's MNIST RG-se R² changes from 0.86 to 0.84, alongside the model revision. Table 3 corrects several R² values to match Table 1, including RG-s from 0.948 to 0.868.

T1.justification: Beyond Equation 11's normalization, Appendix A.1 corrects matrix-product transposes in Equations 13–14, and v1's Gauss–Markov minimum-variance remark is removed. The two least-squares derivations remain, with propositions relabeled as remarks. The normalization correction is incompletely propagated: Appendix Equation 17 retains the unnormalized sums.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the approximation-superiority claim from Wormhole to classical methods and adds robustness across intra-class and inter-class settings. The central contributions—few-shot regression on sliced distances, two linear models, and accelerated RG-Wormhole training—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes poor Sinkhorn performance potentially to regularization choice, interprets class-transfer degradation as moderate, and argues that dataset-dependent coefficient patterns preclude universal fixed weights. These add substantive qualifications and applicability interpretations while retaining the original explanations of data efficiency and RG-Wormhole.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability footnote with a repository address, documents the new baseline tuning grid, and reports a 2.891-second RG calibration cost excluded from inference timings. It also clarifies sample-count notation and corrects B.5's dataset description to acknowledge the already depicted ShapeNetV2 embedding experiment. Existing Wormhole implementation details largely remain.

R1.justification: The new classical-method comparison expands positioning beyond learned Wasserstein embeddings. The Johnson–Wichern reference disappears with the Gauss–Markov remark; most other cited works remain. The updated publication information for Nguyen's sliced-transport introduction identifies the same work, rather than a new citation.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include local explanatory additions, revised sample notation, propositions renamed as remarks, Appendix A renamed from Proofs to Details, and three added experimental subsections. References move before the supplement, with author-year citations and revised author/header text.

P2.justification: v2 adds two comparison tables and ten figures containing transfer scatterplots and coefficient bar charts. It also adopts the ICLR layout throughout, changing typography, margins, headers, and float placement. Figure 1 receives revised vector labels, and constrained RG-se/RG-seo panels in Figures 6, 8, 10, and 12 are redrawn; most other existing graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence against classical baselines and under class-distribution shifts, documents dataset-specific weights, supplies code access information, and reconciles Table 3 with Table 1. These improve evaluation and consistency. However, conflicting test-pair counts in B.6, dataset labels and pair-count descriptions in B.7, and the mismatch between Equations 11 and 17 limit the reliability gains. The net improvement is supported but limited.
